None. `internal/config/config.go` and `config_test.go` are where the work order
said.

None. The unknown-key error keeps its existing wording and now names every
rejected key, comma-separated.

## What the next session must know

- `meta.Keys()` includes key groups, so a nested key fails the `len(key) != 1`
  check and its dotted `key.String()` is reported. `Undecoded` is no longer
  used.
- `DESIGN.md` already promises an unknown key is an error and lists the three
  lowercase keys, so no design change was needed.

1.6.handover:
# 1.6 Preserve each parsed Next item's line terminator

## What landed

- `next: preserve each item's line ending` — `Item` now retains its own
  terminator; `Parse` records it from the source line. `Render` writes each
  parsed item's terminator, supplies the file's detected style when an item is
  not the final output line and has none, and preserves the absent final
  newline. `Add`, `Remove`, `Move` and prose gathering are unchanged.
- `TestRoundTripMixedLineEndings` covers LF-then-CRLF, CRLF-then-LF and a
  missing final newline. `TestMoveMixedLineEndings` covers moving to the ends,
  adding in the middle, and moving a final unterminated item so it gains a
  terminator without welding.

## Landmark drift

None. The evidence lines moved as expected: `Item` is at
`internal/next/next.go:20`, `Parse` at 50, `Render` at 127.

## Deviations from the work order

- The terminator is an unexported `term string` on `Item`, not an exported
  field. It keeps `Item` comparable (existing tests compare values) and stops
  `board` from constructing items with a stale terminator; new items correctly
  fall back to the file style.
- No DESIGN change: the specified format and commands are unchanged; the fix
  preserves bytes the design already says are kept.

## What the next session must know

- `Render` treats the last item as the final output line only when no tail
  lines follow. If the source had no final newline, the final output line is
  rendered without one even when that item carried a terminator from an
  earlier position; this preserves the existing missing-final-newline behavior.
- Terminators are carried by `Move` and by `Remove` because the `Item` value
  moves intact. `Add`/`AddAt` receive items with an empty term, which `Render`
  fills with `n.nl`, detected from the first newline in the source.
- Tests live in `internal/next/next_test.go`.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

commits: b040e35e04de36fe2c2117bf9c6316bb362a8472 repo: report git failures outside the outside-repo case
2.2.handover:
# 2.2 Surface repository failures without breaking operation outside git

## What landed

- `repo: report git failures outside the outside-repo case` — the git runner
  now sets `LC_ALL=C`, captures stderr and returns a `gitError` carrying the
  command, stderr and process error. Only stderr beginning
  `fatal: not a git repository` is classified as the outside-repo case; `Find`
  then returns the worktree hits without error. Every other branch-enumeration
  failure is propagated with its diagnostic.
- Cancellation before a command start returns `ctx.Err()` directly.
- New tests: `TestFindCorruptRefsReturnsError` (malformed packed-refs),
  `TestFindDoesNotSuppressOtherFailures` (pre-cancelled context and no `git` on
  `PATH`). `TestFindOutsideRepository` is unchanged and still passes.
- DESIGN §5 documents `LC_ALL=C`, retained stderr, the exact outside-repo
  diagnostic, and propagation of all other failures.

## Landmark drift

Evidence cited `internal/repo/repo.go:63-75,98-103`; after unit 2.1 the runner is
at the `New` literal (now ~64-95), `Find` at ~97 and `branches` at ~145.

## Deviations from the work order

- Added `withoutLocale`, which removes an inherited `LC_ALL` before appending
  `LC_ALL=C`. On Unix a duplicate `LC_ALL` is not reliably overridden.
- The cancellation test cancels before the call; that exercises the explicit
  `ctx.Err()` pre-check. Cancellation mid-command still propagates the process
  error (typically `signal: killed`), not necessarily `context.Canceled`.
- On a non-outside-repo failure `Find` returns the partial worktree map along
  with the error; callers in `lint` and `cmd` discard the map when err != nil.

## What the next session must know

- `errNotRepository` is package-private and matched via `errors.Is` through
  `gitError.Is`. Do not switch to matching exit code 128; other fatal errors
  also use 128.
- `gitError.Unwrap` preserves the original `*exec.ExitError` / `*exec.Error`, so
  `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` only holds for the pre-check path.
- `New` is the only place the command environment is built; test wrappers that
  replace `r.run` bypass the locale and stderr behavior.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None for this unit. The plan's next stage unit (2.3, lint) is not started.

5.7.handover:
# 5.7 handover

## What landed

- `a6d33a6` — `tui: reload configuration with the workbench`.
  `reload` now calls `config.Load` at `m.board.Root` before `board.Load`, so
  explicit `r`, post-operation reloads and editor-exit reloads all see config
  edits. A valid config replaces `dir`, `kinds` and `areas`; a changed `dir`
  loads the new workbench and later writes go there. Selection stays on the same
  slug when the new workbench still has it.
- `reload` takes a `saved bool`. On invalid config, an explicit/editor reload
  returns the config error before loading, preserving the prior board, derived
  data and config. A reload after a successful board operation falls back to the
  last coherent config, publishes the disk (so the saved change shows), then
  returns the config error; callers keep the `change saved; reload failed:` and
  `reload failed:` prefixes.
- DESIGN §9 describes config reloads and the invalid-config saved-change case;
  §10 records the TUI's read-only `config` dependency. TUI fixtures now write
  `.benchpress.toml` and load it through `config.Load`.
- New tests `TestReloadReadsConfiguration`, `TestReloadSwitchesConfiguredDirectory`
  and `TestReloadInvalidConfiguration`; all three failed before the change.

## Landmark drift

- `reload` moved from `actions.go:72` to `actions.go:76` and its call sites are
  `actions.go:66`, `model.go:165` and `model.go:233`. The cited
  `cmd/benchpress/ls.go:62-66` still loads config per command.
- No other landmark moved. No dependency or go.mod change, so no Nix run.

## Deviations from the work order

- D6's "After a successful operation, also attempt a disk load" is expressed as
  an explicit `saved` argument to `reload`, because the same method serves the
  explicit and editor paths, which must preserve prior data on an invalid
  config instead of publishing the disk.

## What the next session must know

- `reload` returns the config error before plan/lint errors when both occur.
  Lint still runs after a saved-change load under the old config, so the summary
  reflects the published disk rather than `lint unavailable`.
- Config is read at `m.board.Root`, never rediscovered. Tests that construct a
  `board.Board` directly must still create `.benchpress.toml` for reloads to
  succeed; production no longer defaults a missing file.
- `change` remains the only caller passing `true`; editor exits and `r` pass
